question: What distinguishes generative AI from other kinds of AI?
options: It produces new content from a prompt
It classifies data into known categories
It detects anomalies in a stream
It forecasts a number from historical data
explanation: The other three are traditional AI tasks. Generation is what makes drafting, summarising and ideation possible.

question: Which business need is the poorest fit for generative AI?
options: Forecasting next quarter's revenue from historical figures
Drafting a first version of a policy document
Summarising a long research report
Generating ideas for a campaign
explanation: Numeric forecasting from history is classical machine learning. Choosing the wrong technique for the problem is the most common early mistake.

question: What is a pretrained model?
options: A model already trained on broad data before you use it
A model trained exclusively on your company's data
A model that trains itself during each conversation
A model that requires no compute to run
explanation: Pretrained models are the default starting point. Adapting them to your business is a separate decision.

question: A model does not know about your company's products. Which is usually the cheaper and faster remedy?
options: Grounding it in your content at request time
Fine-tuning the model on your data
Training a new model from scratch
Waiting for the next model release
explanation: Grounding supplies the knowledge when the question is asked. Fine-tuning changes the model itself and costs far more for what is usually a knowledge gap.

question: What is fine-tuning best suited to?
options: Teaching a model a consistent style or behaviour
Giving a model today's sales figures
Reducing the number of tokens in a prompt
Encrypting data in transit
explanation: Fine-tuning shapes how a model responds. For facts that change, grounding is the right tool because retraining cannot keep up.

question: What is a token in the context of generative AI cost?
options: A unit of text that is metered going in and coming out
A security credential for the API
A licence assigned to one user
A record of a completed conversation
explanation: Tokens are the billing unit. Prompt length, grounding payload and answer length all convert directly into cost.

question: Which change would most reduce the token cost of a solution?
options: Sending less grounding context with each request
Increasing the maximum response length
Adding more example conversations to every prompt
Switching to a larger model
explanation: Context is often the largest part of a request. Every other option increases the number of tokens processed.

question: An ROI case for an AI solution should be set against what?
options: Total cost of ownership
The licence price alone
The cost of the largest available model
Last year's IT budget
explanation: Usage, integration, oversight and change management all belong in the case. Licence price is the smallest part of most deployments.

question: How should a leader describe the risk of fabrications to a sceptical board?
options: A known property of the technology that must be managed with verification
A defect that the next model release will remove
A problem only affecting free tools
A risk that disappears once data is grounded
explanation: Grounding reduces fabrication but does not eliminate it. Presenting it as a managed risk is both accurate and more credible than promising it away.

question: Where does bias in a generative AI system most commonly originate?
options: The data the model was trained on
The programming language used to call it
The region the model is hosted in
The number of users on the licence
explanation: Models reflect their training data. That is why representative data and evaluation are governance concerns, not just technical ones.

question: Which characteristic makes a business process a good candidate for generative AI?
options: It is repetitive, language-heavy and currently manual
It requires a legally binding signature
It depends on a single numeric calculation
It is performed once a year by one person
explanation: Volume plus language is where the value concentrates. A rare task offers little return however well AI performs it.

question: What does prompt engineering most directly affect?
options: The quality and consistency of the output
The price per token
The region the model runs in
The number of licences required
explanation: Stating the role, format, constraints and an example measurably improves results without changing anything about the model.

question: What does retrieval-augmented generation do?
options: Retrieves relevant content first, then answers from it
Retrains the model on each new document
Compresses the model to run on a laptop
Replaces the need for a prompt
explanation: RAG is retrieval followed by generation. It makes answers current and citable without touching the model's weights.

question: Why is data quality a first-order concern for a grounded AI solution?
options: The model answers from the retrieved content, so poor content produces poor answers
Poor data increases the licence cost
Poor data prevents the model from being deployed
Poor data slows down the network
explanation: Grounding makes your content the source of truth. Stale or contradictory documents become stale or contradictory answers.

question: Which is a genuine business requirement for grounding?
options: Answers must cite internal sources users can open
Answers must always be under 100 words
The model must run in a single region
The solution must avoid using prompts
explanation: Traceability to an internal source is the reason most organisations ground in the first place.

question: When does classical machine learning add more value than generative AI?
options: Predicting a numeric outcome from structured historical data
Drafting a customer email
Summarising a set of meeting notes
Generating campaign imagery
explanation: Prediction over structured history is what machine learning is for. Knowing which technique fits is a leadership judgment, not a technical one.

question: Which stage comes first in the lifecycle of a machine learning solution?
options: Defining the problem and preparing data
Deploying the model to production
Monitoring model drift
Retraining on new data
explanation: Everything downstream depends on a well-framed problem and usable data. Monitoring and retraining come after deployment.

question: Which is a security consideration specific to AI systems rather than software generally?
options: Defending against prompt manipulation
Applying operating system patches
Rotating TLS certificates
Configuring firewall rules
explanation: Prompt manipulation is the attack surface AI introduces. The rest are standard practice that continues to apply.

question: Why is scalability often cited as a business benefit of generative AI?
options: The same capability can serve many people at once without proportional headcount
It removes the need to measure outcomes
It guarantees lower licence costs
It eliminates the need for governance
explanation: Serving more demand without adding people is the economic argument. It does not remove the need to measure or govern.

question: Which two are genuine limitations of generative AI that leaders should plan around? Choose two.
options: It can produce fluent answers that are wrong
It can reflect bias present in its training data
It cannot process text in more than one language
It cannot be used with private company data
explanation: Fabrication and inherited bias are real and persistent. Multilingual support and grounding on private data are both well established.

question: Which two increase the cost of a generative AI request? Choose two.
options: A longer grounding payload
A longer generated answer
A shorter system message
Fewer users on the tenant
explanation: Tokens are counted going in and coming out, so both context size and answer length drive cost. User count affects licensing, not per-request metering.

question: Match each approach to adapting a model with what it does.

pairs.definition: Change the instruction to change the output
Supply your own content at request time
Adapt the model itself with your examples
Build a new model from raw data

explanation: The list runs from cheapest and fastest to most expensive. Working down it in order is the sensible default.

question: Match each AI challenge to its description.

pairs.definition: A confident answer that is not true
Skew inherited from training data
Inconsistent quality across similar requests
People accepting output without checking

explanation: Three are properties of the system and one is a property of its users. Governance has to address both kinds.

question: What grounds licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot in your organisation's own data?
options: Microsoft Graph
Azure Resource Manager
Microsoft Entra Connect
Power Automate
explanation: Graph is the layer holding the relationships between people, files, meetings and messages. It is what makes an answer specific to your business.

question: Where should mapping a business process to Copilot begin?
options: With the app the work already happens in
With the largest available model
With the licensing agreement
With the datacenter region
explanation: Adoption follows existing habits. If the work happens in Outlook, that is where Copilot should first appear.

question: Which Copilot capability best fits summarising a long email thread?
options: Copilot in Outlook
Copilot in Excel
Copilot Studio
Azure AI Search
explanation: Match the surface to the content. Threads live in Outlook, so that is where the summary belongs.

question: Which Copilot capability best fits analysing a table of sales figures?
options: Copilot in Excel
Copilot in Word
Copilot in Outlook
Copilot Pages
explanation: Analysis belongs where the data model and formulas already are.

question: What is the main difference between Copilot Chat and licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot?
options: What organisational data each is able to reach
The language each supports
The device each runs on
The colour of the interface
explanation: Grounding in tenant data through Graph is the dividing line, and it is what the licence buys.

question: A task requires multi-step investigation across many internal and external sources. Which should you use?
options: Researcher
Analyst
Copilot in PowerPoint
Azure AI Search alone
explanation: Researcher is built for sustained investigation across sources rather than a single question and answer.

question: A task requires reasoning over a dataset to produce charts and figures. Which should you use?
options: Analyst
Researcher
Copilot in Outlook
Copilot Pages
explanation: Analyst is the data-reasoning agent. Researcher investigates; Analyst calculates.

question: Which tool builds custom agents with low code?
options: Microsoft Copilot Studio
Microsoft Excel
Azure Resource Manager
Microsoft Purview
explanation: Copilot Studio is the low-code authoring surface for agents, topics, knowledge and actions.

question: An existing Copilot works well but lacks knowledge of your product catalogue. Which option is usually cheapest?
options: Extend Copilot with the missing knowledge
Build a new agent from scratch
Buy a third-party assistant
Fine-tune a custom model
explanation: Extending suits a knowledge gap. Building is for when the required behaviour, not just the knowledge, is different.

question: When is building a custom agent the right choice over extending Copilot?
options: When the required behaviour and workflow differ from Copilot's
When you only need to add a document library
When you want a different interface colour
When you want to reduce licence count
explanation: Behaviour is the dividing line. If only the knowledge is missing, extension is less work and less to maintain.

question: What does the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework let you do?
options: Add capability to the existing Copilot rather than replacing it
Remove Copilot from selected users
Reduce the token cost of every request
Deploy Copilot to an on-premises server
explanation: Extensibility keeps one assistant that users already know and widens what it can reach and do.

question: Which Foundry capability provides retrieval over your indexed content?
options: Azure AI Search
Azure Monitor
Azure Policy
Azure Bastion
explanation: Azure AI Search is the retrieval half of a retrieval-augmented generation solution.

question: When choosing a model for a business need, which is the sensible default?
options: The smallest model that reliably does the job
The largest model available
The newest model released
The model with the longest context window
explanation: Capability, latency and cost trade against each other. Reaching for the largest model by default wastes money and adds delay.

question: Which need points toward Foundry Tools rather than Microsoft 365 Copilot?
options: Building a custom AI application for customers
Summarising internal meeting notes
Drafting an internal memo
Recapping a Teams call
explanation: Foundry is the pro-code platform for building applications. Copilot serves work already happening inside Microsoft 365.

question: What is the model catalogue in Microsoft Foundry?
options: The set of models available to choose between
A record of every request made
A list of licensed users
A billing statement
explanation: The catalogue is where model selection begins, offering Microsoft and third-party models side by side.

question: Which is a genuine risk-mitigation benefit of an integrated Microsoft AI solution?
options: Consistent identity, permissions and compliance controls across services
Guaranteed factual accuracy of every response
Elimination of all licence costs
Automatic approval of AI use cases
explanation: Integration means one identity and compliance story rather than several. It does not make output true.

question: A department wants Copilot to answer from a SharePoint library of policies. What is required?
options: The content must be reachable and the users must have permission to it
The policies must be rewritten as prompts
Each user must have a Foundry subscription
The library must be made public
explanation: Copilot answers within each user's permissions. Making content public would be a security failure, not a prerequisite.

question: Which describes Microsoft Graph in one sentence?
options: The connected view of people, files, meetings and messages in a tenant
A charting library for reports
A network monitoring service
A model training platform
explanation: Graph is the relationship layer across Microsoft 365, which is exactly what makes grounded answers possible.

question: Which factor should drive the choice between building, buying and extending?
options: Whether the gap is knowledge or behaviour
Whether the vendor offers a discount
Which option was chosen last time
Which team has spare capacity
explanation: Knowledge gaps are met by extending or grounding; behaviour gaps need a purpose-built agent. Framing it this way keeps the decision technical rather than political.

question: Which two capabilities does Microsoft Copilot Studio provide? Choose two.
options: Building agents with low code
Adding knowledge sources to an agent
Provisioning virtual machines
Managing Microsoft 365 licences
explanation: Copilot Studio authors agents and the knowledge behind them. Infrastructure and licensing are handled elsewhere.

question: Which two are benefits of Microsoft Foundry for building AI applications? Choose two.
options: A choice of models to suit different needs
Scalable, secure hosting for the solution
Automatic writing of your business requirements
Guaranteed elimination of model bias
explanation: Model choice and managed scale are real platform benefits. No platform writes your requirements or removes bias for you.

question: Match each Microsoft AI capability to what it is for.

pairs.definition: Assist with work inside Microsoft 365 apps
Build custom agents with low code
Build AI applications with pro-code tools
Ground answers in tenant data

explanation: The three products sit on a ladder from ready-made to fully custom. Graph is not a product on that ladder but the data layer beneath them.

question: Match each task to the most suitable Microsoft AI option.

pairs.definition: Researcher

pairs.term: Reasoning over data to produce charts
pairs.definition: Analyst
An agent built in Copilot Studio
Microsoft Foundry

explanation: The first two are ready-made agents, the third is low-code and the fourth is pro-code. Picking the least custom option that works is the usual right answer.

question: Why should responsible AI be treated as a leadership responsibility?
options: It requires decisions about acceptable use that only leaders can authorise
It is purely a technical configuration task
It is required to obtain a licence
It reduces the number of models needed
explanation: Responsible AI is a set of decisions about what the organisation will and will not do. Those need authority behind them.

question: What is the role of an AI council?
options: To guide strategy, oversight and cross-functional alignment
To write the code for AI solutions
To purchase hardware
To answer end-user support tickets
explanation: The council sets direction and arbitrates. Delivery and support sit with other teams.

question: Which is a governance principle rather than a technical control?
options: Deciding which AI use cases require review before launch
Enabling multifactor authentication
Configuring a network security group
Rotating an API key
explanation: Governance is about who decides and on what basis. The other three are implementations that follow such decisions.

question: Which is a common barrier to AI adoption inside an organisation?
options: Employees fearing the effect on their jobs
The absence of a public cloud region
A shortage of physical office space
Too many available models
explanation: Adoption barriers are usually human: fear, no clear use case, no sponsorship and no time to learn.

question: What does an AI champions programme do?
options: Spreads capability peer to peer across teams
Replaces the need for governance
Manages the licensing budget
Writes the organisation's AI code
explanation: Champions work because colleagues learn fastest from the person sitting next to them showing a real example.

question: What distinguishes an adoption team from an AI council?
options: The adoption team runs the rollout; the council sets direction
The adoption team writes policy; the council runs training
They are two names for the same group
The adoption team owns the budget; the council owns the code
explanation: One decides what is allowed and why; the other makes it happen in practice. Merging them tends to leave neither job done.

question: A pilot has strong sponsorship but low usage, and users say they have no time to learn. What should you address?
options: Provide dedicated time and practical examples
Purchase additional licences
Switch to a larger model
Reduce the number of use cases to zero
explanation: Name the actual barrier and treat that one. Buying more of something nobody has time to use makes the problem worse.

question: Which Copilot licence arrangement suits an organisation with steady, widespread daily usage?
options: A per-user monthly subscription
Pay-as-you-go consumption
A one-off perpetual purchase
No licence at all
explanation: Predictable broad usage suits per-user subscription. Pay-as-you-go suits sporadic or concentrated usage.

question: Which Foundry Tools arrangement suits predictable high volume?
options: A commitment tier
Pay-as-you-go
A trial subscription
A per-device licence
explanation: Commitment tiers trade flexibility for a better rate, which only pays off when volume is genuinely predictable.

question: Beyond licence cost, which impact should be assessed before a broad AI rollout?
options: Effects on data, security and privacy
The colour scheme of the interface
The number of meeting rooms available
The age of the organisation's logo
explanation: Widening who can reach content through AI surfaces existing data and permission problems, so those belong in the assessment.

question: Which two belong in the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard? Choose two.
options: Fairness
Transparency
Profitability
Market share
explanation: The standard covers fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency and accountability. Commercial measures are not among them.

question: Which two help overcome resistance to AI adoption? Choose two.
options: Visible sponsorship from leadership
Peer champions demonstrating real use cases
Mandating usage targets without training
Removing all governance requirements
explanation: Sponsorship and peer proof both build confidence. Mandates without support and ungoverned rollout each generate more resistance, not less.

question: Match each responsible AI principle to what it requires.

pairs.definition: Treat all groups of people equitably
Make it clear how the system decides
Ensure people remain answerable for outcomes
Work for people of all abilities

explanation: Accountability is the principle that keeps a person responsible for what the system does, which is why governance needs named owners.

question: Match each adoption element to its role.

pairs.definition: Set strategy and provide oversight
Run the rollout day to day
Spread capability among peers
Give the programme visible authority

explanation: Four distinct jobs: decide, deliver, spread and back. Programmes usually fail because one of the four has no owner.
